title: Invertibility of the explicitly curried restricted evaluation
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and U any open, with derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] of module sheaves on X, each over-site and U in a common localization universe. Let R be exact restriction followed by the canonical over equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Let H and HU be the shared derived internal Homs [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and eX,eU the canonical tensor-Hom equivalences [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection]. For ANY bifunctorially natural family of isomorphisms t(K,L):R(K tensor L)≅R(K) tensor R(L), and any L,E, the map m(L,E)=eU.symm(t(H(L,E),L).inv; R(eX(identity of H(L,E)))) from R(H(L,E)) to HU(R(L),R(E)) is invertible. The map is explicitly prescribed; the conclusion asserts only invertibility, not existence of comparison families or compatibility for arbitrary maps.

proof.text: Use exact extension by zero J, transported from the over-site to U, and its derived adjunction J ⊣ R. Its unit is invertible: on U restriction of extension by zero is the identity. Its essential image consists of complexes with zero cohomology stalks outside U; the adjunction counit is invertible on these complexes. Exactness permits termwise extension by zero and transports these assertions to derived categories.

Choose a K-flat representative for L using lem-pc-kflat-resolution; compare the derived tensor with its total tensor model by lem-pc-kflat-derived-tensor-comparison (and symmetry if the K-flat factor is second). For A on U, J(A) tensor L is supported on U by lem-sc-derived-tensor-stalk-vanishing. Thus the adjoint of eta_A tensor identity followed by t(J(A),L).inv is an isomorphism J(A tensor R(L)) -> J(A) tensor L. Its adjunction image is invertible, since eta_A and t are invertible; invertibility of eta_(A tensor R(L)) then makes its restriction invertible. Both objects are U-supported, and restriction reflects isomorphisms between such objects by stalks. The empty-open and zero-factor cases are included.

For f:A -> R(H(L,E)), let q:J(A) -> H(L,E) be its adjoint. Precomposition by the tensor isomorphism, under the adjunction and tensor-Hom bijections, gives the transpose of (unit_A tensor identity);t(J(A),L).inv;R(eX(q)). First-variable tensor-Hom naturality expresses eX(q)=(q tensor identity);eX(identity). Tensor naturality for (q,identity) moves R(q tensor identity) past t.inv, and unit_A;R(q)=f gives (f tensor identity);t(H(L,E),L).inv;R(eX(identity)). The definition of m and tensor-Hom naturality on U identify this with eU(f;m). Thus postcomposition by m is a composite of five bijections, hence bijective for every A. Yoneda implies m is invertible.
